tos.title: Terms of Use
tos.subtitle: Read and accept before continuing. These terms govern your use of this Overture instance.

auth.heading: Authentication
auth.body: The package determines the authentication mode: standard Cloudflare OAuth, or a Cloudflare API token you create and paste yourself. Either way, the credential is handled server-side and never reaches this page's JavaScript. A pasted token becomes the app's own long-lived credential, written into the deployed app unchanged and scoped to exactly the permissions the app's creation link requested — Overture neither mints nor deletes it.

privacy.heading: No Data Retention
privacy.body: Overture keeps no logs and retains no record of what was deployed, by whom, or when. No information about your usage is transmitted to or stored by the operator of this instance.

ownership.heading: Account Ownership and Billing
ownership.body: All resources are created within your own Cloudflare account. You are responsible for all associated costs. Overture holds no ownership of anything it deploys on your behalf.

liability.heading: Deployment Liability
liability.body: You bear full responsibility for every deployment made through this tool and for all consequences that follow. Overture is an automated executor of your instructions and assumes no liability for outcomes.

capabilities.heading: Package Capabilities
capabilities.body: Any package this instance of Overture accepts may exercise, within your Cloudflare account, any capability it declares. The wizard presents a complete disclosure of those capabilities before you authorize any deployment.

license.heading: License and Availability
license.body: Overture's own code is AGPL-3.0-or-later; the distributed package incorporates GPL-3.0 components, making the combined work AGPL-3.0. Source code is publicly available. Overture is never sold; any offer of paid access is fraudulent.

analyze.title: What this package will do
analyze.failed: The package could not be read
analyze.summaryFindings: Read the points below before you go on.
analyze.certain: The script was read end to end, so the lists below are everything it can reach.
analyze.uncertainScan: The script decides part of what it does while running, so the lists below are what could be read — not a promise that nothing else happens.
analyze.permissionsIntro: What this app must be allowed to do in your Cloudflare account.
analyze.permissionsNone: None — nothing here needs a permission of its own.
analyze.checksTitle: Account checks the package asks for
analyze.checkUnknown: not an endpoint this deployer allows — the check cannot pass
analyze.checkMalformed: not a usable API path — the check cannot run
analyze.networkIntro: The script sends these itself. It never holds your credentials, but anything it has worked out can leave this way.
analyze.networkOpaque: {count} network call(s) build their address while running, so where they go could not be read.

findings.scriptUnparsed: This package's script is not valid JavaScript, so nothing about it could be read: {detail}
findings.undeclaredCapability: The script calls {methods}, but the package never declares the “{capability}” capability. Those calls are refused part-way through the deployment.
findings.unusedCapability: The package asks for the “{capability}” capability and the script never uses it.
findings.unusedCapabilityUncertain: The package asks for the “{capability}” capability and no use of it was found — though this script hides part of what it does.
findings.malformedCheckPath: The “{check}” check names a path the wizard will not send: {path}
findings.unknownCheckEndpoint: The “{check}” check points at {path}, which this deployer does not allow. It will be refused rather than reach Cloudflare.
findings.checkTokenUnresolved: The “{check}” check still carries the placeholder {token}, which nothing fills in — it is sent as written.
findings.ownNetwork: The script contacts {count} address(es) of its own: {hosts}
findings.opaqueNetwork: {count} of the script's network calls build their address while running, so where they go could not be read.
findings.dynamicCode: The script tries to turn data into code while it runs. That's not allowed — only the code that shipped in the package can run — so those attempts fail.
findings.computedAccess: Part of the script decides at runtime which action to call, so this analysis may not have caught everything it does.
findings.hostSecretCredential: The deployed app is given your {source} and keeps it for as long as it stays deployed.
findings.hostSecretAccountId: The deployed app is given your Cloudflare account ID.
findings.passwordInVar: The value of “{input}” is written into the plain Worker variable {var}, where anyone with dashboard access can read it.
findings.adoptsExisting: This app looks for resources it already owns in your account ({resources}) and writes into them instead of creating new ones.
findings.oauthScopeUnderReported: The script appears to need {scopes}, but the package's declared permissions don't cover them, so those permissions are never requested when you sign in. Those calls are refused part-way through the deployment.
findings.oauthScopeOverReported: The package's declared permissions ask for {scopes}, and the script never uses them.
findings.oauthScopeBeyondCeiling: This app's Sign in with Cloudflare would need {scopes}, which this Overture instance's sign-in was not set up to grant. Sign-in is not offered for this app; it installs with a token you paste instead.
findings.paidCheckManualOauth: Cloudflare OAuth cannot read billing. In Sign in with Cloudflare mode, the paid-plan requirement will require your explicit confirmation rather than an automatic verification.

uncertain.writeAssumed: Cloudflare also lists the read-only group here, but what this app does needs write access.
uncertain.zoneMayBeNeeded: Attaching a custom domain also touches the zone's DNS and certificate, so a zone-level permission may be needed as well.

authMethod.title: Choose how to connect
authMethod.subtitle: Pick how this app gets permission to work in your Cloudflare account.

oauth.title: Standard
oauth.description: Sign in with your Cloudflare account. It's the simplest option — nothing to create or paste.

auto.title: Token
auto.description: Create a Cloudflare token using a link that already has the right permissions and app name filled in, then paste it in.

notAvailable.title: This app can't connect here
notAvailable.body: This app can only be connected using Sign in with Cloudflare, and this Overture instance hasn't been configured for it. There's nothing you can do here — try a different Overture instance, or ask whoever runs this one to set it up.
notAvailable.scopeShortfall: This app needs Cloudflare permissions that this Overture instance's Sign in with Cloudflare was not set up to grant: {scopes}. It declares no other way to connect, so it can't be installed here — try a different Overture instance, or ask whoever runs this one to widen its sign-in.

authorize.appScopesNone: None — this app needs no permissions of its own.
authorize.hostScopesIntro: This deployer's own baseline — the same permissions every time, whichever app you picked:
authorize.popupBlocked: Your browser's popup blocker stopped the sign-in window from opening. Allow popups for this site, then try again.
authorize.grantedUnknown: Couldn't read the token's permissions back — it may not include the API Tokens read above. That's fine; the deploy still works.
authorize.accountsHelp: Pick the Cloudflare account this should be installed into.
authorize.checksHelp: Requirements checked before anything is created. A paid-plan check is automatic with a token, and needs your confirmation when Cloudflare OAuth cannot read billing.
authorize.paidManualHelp: Cloudflare OAuth cannot read billing. Open Billing, confirm that this account has an active paid subscription, then acknowledge it here. Overture does not verify this result in OAuth mode.
authorize.paidManualConfirm: I confirm that this account has an active paid subscription.
authorize.r2KeysPairRequired: Provide both R2 key fields, or leave both empty.
authorize.blocked: Something the package requires isn't satisfied yet. Fix the rows marked above, then re-check.

auto.title: Create an Account API Token
auto.subtitle: Follow the link below to create an Account API Token on Cloudflare, then paste it here. User API Tokens are not accepted.
auto.intro: This token deploys the app, and if the app needs a long-term credential afterward, this same token becomes it. Nothing is deleted or swapped out later — it stays your own token, and you can remove it from your Cloudflare dashboard whenever you want.
auto.tokenRequired: This app needs its own token to write as a Worker Secret. Paste it again to continue; the existing value is never shown.
auto.tokenLinkLabel: Create the pre-named Account API Token on Cloudflare
auto.requirementsIntro: Required permissions can't be removed; optional ones you can uncheck.
auto.checkPermissionsIntro: These are added automatically and used only for the read-only checks that run before Overture creates anything.
auto.overtureReadNote: Lets Overture confirm which permissions your token ended up with once you paste it. Read-only: it cannot create or delete tokens.
auto.dangerIntro: This app is asking for permissions that most apps never need — things like managing tokens, billing, or account settings. Make sure you trust this app before creating a token with them:

policy.title: Deployment policy
policy.subtitle: Which repositories this Overture will accept a deploy package from.
policy.riskBody: With the allowlist off, this Overture will fetch and run a deploy package from any GitHub repository a visitor names — that package can still only do what its declared capabilities allow, but inside the visitor's own Cloudflare account.
policy.readOnlyHint: This page only displays the policy in effect. To change it, edit ALLOWLIST_ENABLED / ALLOWED_SOURCES in this deployment's wrangler.toml and redeploy the Worker.
